surveys.title: Before we go any further — Your brand
questions: What does the word "brand" mean to you?
How would you describe your brand?
What have you done to build your brand?
How would someone else depict your brand?

surveys.title: Brand Personified
questions: Hands (hard work, effort, determination) — How does this relate to YOUR business?
Brain — How does strategy or thinking relate to your brand?
Eyes — What is your brand's vision?
Mouth — How does your brand communicate?
Heart — What passion or values drive your brand?
Feet — What moves your brand forward or grounds it?

surveys.title: Branding reflection
questions: What is a brand?
What do certain colors and fonts communicate to customers?
What makes a good tagline?
Write down five things you learned.

surveys.title: Brand check-in
questions: What does the word "brand" mean to you?
How would you describe your brand?
What have you done to build your brand?
How would someone else depict your brand?
Have your answers changed from the beginning of class? Why or why not?

surveys.title: Putting In Work — "About Me"
questions: Write the "About Me" section for your future or current social media pages and website.

surveys.title: Research — Competition
questions: Make a list of every company you can find (5–10 preferably) that provides the same thing your business (or business idea) provides; these companies could potentially be your competition.

surveys.title: Business Canvas — Branding section
questions: Go to your business canvas and answer the corresponding questions on sticky notes in the Branding section. Then type out a paragraph of those responses in your Business Synopsis.

surveys.title: Pitches
questions: Write your 100-word pitch. Include a concise idea about what your business is, who you serve, and how we can contact you. You can continue to refine your 40-word pitch as well.

questions.question: What does Allen Woods define as a "brand" in The Studio panel discussion?
questions.optionA: A logo or visual representation of a company
questions.optionB: Your logo and a collection of elements, memories, or emotions that connect you to an entity/company

questions.question: How does Ray Ball recommend approaching networking in The Studio panel discussion?
questions.optionA: Only attending typical mixer-style networking events
questions.optionB: Attending events with people who can help you win, being strategic about your time, and noticing customers in non-traditional settings
questions.optionC: Avoid networking until your brand is perfect

questions.question: What percentage of communication is your tone of voice and body language?
What is mirroring while communicating?
questions.optionA: Mirroring the body language of the person you're talking to
questions.optionB: Talking to yourself in the mirror
